Lessons.Title: Angle Measurement and Perpendicular Lines
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 Grade 4 Unit 7 Lesson 10 — Angle Measurement and Perpendicular Lines: practise measuring actual angles with a protractor; lines that intersect at exactly a right angle (90°) are perpendicular. The previous lesson introduced 1° = 1/360 of a turn and the two number scales on a protractor.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Number Talk: Quotients (10 minutes); Activity 1: Angles Here, There, Everywhere (15 minutes); Activity 2: A Folding Challenge (20 minutes); Cool-down: Size Up Angles (5 minutes)

Source warm-up Number Talk: Quotients (10 min) gives FOUR expressions, not only two: 180÷2=90, 180÷4=45, 360÷8=45, 360÷16=22.5. Students explain patterns, halving and structure mentally; do not imply 360÷16 is a whole-number quotient.

Original Activity 1, Angles Here, There, Everywhere (15 min), requires students to PLACE a protractor themselves, not only read one already positioned. They measure standalone angles, then angles marked s,t in a trapezoid, q,r in a rhombus, and e,f at three intersecting lines. Extend short rays when needed, line up protractor centre and zero baseline, read correct scale or subtract two readings on the SAME scale, and check results against a 90° right-angle estimate.

Original Activity 2, A Folding Challenge (20 min), has Tyler ask Lin to create four 90° angles sharing vertex P WITHOUT a protractor. Fold along a crease through P and fold again through P so opposite halves of the first crease coincide. Two perpendicular crease lines then form four right angles: 360°÷4=90°. Pupils trace two distinct perpendicular lines, fold another set through the same point with a different colour, and locate perpendicular sides in source pictured shapes. Physical folding, square-corner checking and original diagrams require teacher review.

First-party Edulytics Cool-down (NOT original publisher Size Up Angles): draw intersecting straight lines through P with one 90° angle; label and explain why the lines are perpendicular and mark all four 90° angles. Teacher checks physical construction. Original gated publisher Cool-down and original figure measurements are not claimed digitized.

Practice routing: REUSE Grade 4 U07:L09 exact protractor reading family for digitally specified zero-aligned measurements; EXTEND existing shared exact engine with a small independently authored numerical perpendicular YES/NO question family for intersections with stated angle degrees. Neither tests original printed pictures nor replaces teacher-assessed paper folding.

KeyConcepts.Title: Measure with a real protractor
KeyConcepts.Definition: Angle measure depends on the turn between rays, not their length or apparent orientation.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Align centre with vertex, align one ray with zero, then read the same calibrated scale. If neither ray meets zero, subtract readings on one scale or realign.
KeyConcepts.Example: A FIRST-PARTY scale description from 35° to 100° on the same scale spans 65°; this is NOT a measured publisher figure.

KeyConcepts.Title: Perpendicular lines
KeyConcepts.Definition: Two lines are perpendicular exactly when they intersect to make a right (90°) angle.
KeyConcepts.Rule: If one intersection angle equals 90°, adjacent angles also measure 90° and all four angles at the intersection are right angles.
KeyConcepts.Example: Two folds through P with equal halves of each 180° straight angle yield four 90° corners.

KeyConcepts.Title: Perpendicular sides in polygons
KeyConcepts.Definition: Two drawn segments can be perpendicular even if their full supporting lines must be extended to locate a 90° corner.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Verify the angle with a protractor or square corner; don't infer perpendicularity from how drawing looks.
KeyConcepts.Example: Trapezoid s,t; rhombus q,r; three-line figure e,f are original source labels, but individual original numeric angle measures are NOT reproduced.

WorkedExamples.Title: All four original Number Talk quotients
WorkedExamples.Question: Find 180÷2, 180÷4, 360÷8 and 360÷16 mentally.

WorkedExamples.Title: A protractor reading for a standalone angle
WorkedExamples.Question: An independently authored protractor scale shows a first ray through 35° and a second through 100° on the same calibrated scale. What is the angle?
WorkedExamples.Method: Subtract the two readings on the SAME scale; or realign starting ray to zero first.
Steps: Both ray crossings are on one scale.
WorkedExamples.Check: Correct for this independent verbal example; does not supply exact original source figure dimensions.

WorkedExamples.Title: Why perpendicular folding makes four right angles
WorkedExamples.Question: Tyler asks Lin to draw four 90° angles through P without a protractor. How can two folds help?
WorkedExamples.Method: First fold creates straight 180° angles. Second fold bisects each 180° angle by aligning the edges of the first crease.
Steps: Fold the first straight crease through point P.
Refold through P so the first-crease edges line up exactly.
Each half of a straight 180° angle is 90°.
Trace perpendicular crease lines; four angles around P total 360°.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Two perpendicular straight creases yield four right angles of 90°.
WorkedExamples.Check: 4×90=360; teacher checks folded accuracy and colour marking.

WorkedExamples.Title: Numerical classification, independently authored
WorkedExamples.Question: At the intersection of two supporting lines, one angle measures 100°. Are they perpendicular?
Steps: A perpendicular intersection forms a right angle of exactly 90°.
Therefore the lines are not perpendicular.
WorkedExamples.Check: A 90° stated angle would instead mean yes (digital code 1).

WorkedExamples.Title: Source polygon labels and physical measurement (teacher-led)
WorkedExamples.Question: Measure original labeled s,t on a trapezoid, q,r on a rhombus and e,f in a three-line intersection; identify any perpendicular sides in original pictured shapes.
WorkedExamples.Method: View actual local 2021 source figures and align physical protractor or straightedge accurately.
Steps: Extend any too-short supporting segments before aligning rays.
Align protractor centre with each labeled vertex, zero with one side.
Read using the correct scale; verify angle size against right-angle benchmark.
Explain whether actual shapes display perpendicular sides using measured 90°.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Source-specific individual results depend on original artwork and teacher measurement.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent Edulytics Cool-down (teacher-reviewed)
WorkedExamples.Question: Draw two perpendicular straight lines meeting at P, mark and measure one 90° angle, and label the other three.
WorkedExamples.Method: Draw and use a protractor or square corner, explain 180° straight halves.
Steps: Draw first straight line through P.
Create another line through P making one 90° corner.
Mark all four right angles; justify 360°÷4=90°.
WorkedExamples.Check: Substitute independent assessment; original publisher Size Up Angles is gated.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating the last Number Talk answer 360÷16 as 45 or 22.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Dividing by 16, not by 8, halves 45 to 22.5.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using one protractor scale's first reading and the other scale's second reading.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Opposing protractor scales are complementary and cannot be subtracted across scales.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Realign initial ray to zero OR subtract two values on the SAME calibrated scale.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming two lines are perpendicular because they seem vertical or horizontal.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Drawing orientation alone does not prove an angle of exactly 90°.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use a real protractor/square corner or precisely constructed folds to verify the right angle.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming perpendicular segments must fully cross as two infinite straight lines.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Polygon sides can meet at a vertex or their supporting lines extend beyond segment endpoints.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Extend supporting lines mentally or with a ruler and inspect their angle.

SummaryPoints: Original source measures labelled polygon s,t and q,r and intersecting-line e,f figures using a physically placed protractor; specific measures remain teacher-scored.
Perpendicular lines intersect at exactly 90°. Two precise folds through P create four 90° sectors.
Reuse the prior exact protractor scale family; new complementary exact perpendicular judgment family only for independently stated numeric angles.
First-party Cool-down: draw and mark four right angles through P; original publisher Size Up Angles remains gated.
Do not assert source visual parity or passing unrun .NET tests.
